source.text: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἐπορεύθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς σάββασιν διὰ τῶν σπορίμων· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασαν καὶ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν.

records.literal_gloss: At that the time went the Jesus on the Sabbaths through the grainfields; the and disciples of him were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.

en.L: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath; and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and to eat.
en.B: About that time Jesus was walking through the fields of grain on a Sabbath day. His disciples were hungry, so they started picking some heads of grain and eating them.
en.R: Around that time, Jesus was walking through some grain fields on the Sabbath, the day of rest. His followers were hungry. So they began to pick some grain and eat it.

fr.L: En ce temps-là, Jésus passa un jour de sabbat à travers les champs de blé ; et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples eurent faim et se mirent à arracher des épis et à manger.
fr.B: Vers ce temps-là, un jour de sabbat, Jésus traversait des champs de blé. Ses disciples avaient faim ; ils se mirent donc à cueillir des épis et à en manger les grains.
fr.R: À cette époque-là, un jour de sabbat, le jour du repos, Jésus marchait à travers des champs de blé. Ses disciples avaient faim. Alors ils ont commencé à cueillir des épis et à en manger les grains.

decisions.choice: plucking grain: allowed in a neighbor's field, but counted as work on the Sabbath
decisions.reason: The law let a hungry traveler pick grain by hand in someone else's field (Deuteronomy 23:25). The question is the day: harvesting was forbidden on the Sabbath (Exodus 34:21), and plucking could be counted as harvesting.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: at that time: the scene follows Jesus's promise of rest (11:28-30)
decisions.reason: Matthew joins the Sabbath stories to the call to find rest in Jesus. The link is one of placement, not of time.

decisions.choice: the day of rest
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Sabbath is.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic present kept at Literal (12:13 "il dit"); speech in the passé composé at every level, David's story (12:3-4) included
decisions.reason: As in John, Mark and Luke: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé the tense of speech and of stories for young readers. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: un jour de sabbat, le sabbat (lowercase) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form: "sabbat" is a common noun in French and takes no capital. The Greek plural names one Sabbath day (m2), so French says "un jour de sabbat". Readable adds "le jour du repos", as the English does.

source.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἰδόντες εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ οἱ μαθηταί σου ποιοῦσιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ποιεῖν ἐν σαββάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Pharisees having seen said to him, Look, the disciples of you are doing what not is lawful to do on Sabbath.

en.L: But the Pharisees, seeing [this], said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on [the] Sabbath."
en.B: The Pharisees saw it and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "See there! Your disciples are doing something that the law forbids on the Sabbath."
en.R: Some Pharisees saw this. They said to Jesus, "Look! Your followers are doing something that is against the law on the Sabbath."

fr.L: Mais les Pharisiens, voyant [cela], {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Regarde, {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} disciples font ce qu’il n’est pas permis de faire un jour de sabbat. »
fr.B: Les Pharisiens le virent et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Vois donc ! Tes disciples font ce que la Loi défend le jour du sabbat. »
fr.R: Des Pharisiens ont vu cela. Ils ont dit à Jésus : « Regarde ! Tes disciples font une chose que la Loi interdit le jour du sabbat. »

decisions.choice: not lawful: forbidden by the law as the Pharisees understood it
decisions.reason: The Pharisees counted plucking grain as the work of harvesting, which the law of Moses forbade on the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: look (L, R); see there (B)
decisions.reason: In speech the word points to something happening in front of them, so it is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε ἐπείνασεν καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: He but said to them, Not have you read what did David when he was hungry and those with him?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him?
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Do you not remember reading what David did when he and the men with him were hungry?
en.R: Jesus answered, "Have you not read about what David did when he and his men were hungry?

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « N’avez-vous pas lu ce qu’a fait David quand il a eu faim, ainsi que ceux [qui étaient] avec lui ?
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Ne vous souvenez-vous pas d’avoir lu ce qu’a fait David quand lui et ses compagnons ont eu faim ?
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Vous n’avez pas lu ce qu’a fait David, un jour où lui et ses hommes avaient faim ?

decisions.choice: what David did: 1 Samuel 21:1-6
decisions.reason: David, fleeing from Saul, asked the priest at Nob for bread and was given the holy bread.

decisions.choice: have you not read: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The Pharisees knew the Scriptures well. Jesus asks whether they have understood what they read.

source.text: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγον, ὃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις;

records.literal_gloss: how he entered into the house of the God and the loaves of the presentation they ate, which not lawful was for him to eat nor for those with him, except for the priests only?

en.L: How he entered the house of God, and they ate the loaves of the presentation, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, but only for the priests?
en.B: He went into the house of God, and they ate the sacred bread set out before God. Neither David nor his men were allowed to eat it; only the priests were.
en.R: David went into the house of God, and they ate the special bread that had been placed there before God. The law did not allow David or his men to eat that bread. Only the priests were allowed to eat it.

fr.L: Comment il est entré dans la maison de Dieu, et [comment] ils ont mangé les pains de la présentation, qu’il ne lui était pas permis de manger, ni à ceux [qui étaient] avec lui, mais aux prêtres seuls ?
fr.B: Il est entré dans la maison de Dieu, et ils ont mangé les pains sacrés présentés devant Dieu. Ni David ni ses hommes n’avaient le droit d’en manger ; seuls les prêtres l’avaient.
fr.R: David est entré dans la maison de Dieu, et ils ont mangé le pain spécial qu’on avait placé là, devant Dieu. La Loi ne permettait ni à David ni à ses hommes de manger ce pain. Seuls les prêtres avaient le droit d’en manger.

decisions.choice: the loaves of the presentation: the twelve loaves set out before God
decisions.reason: Twelve loaves were placed on a table in the holy place each Sabbath and were afterward eaten only by the priests (Leviticus 24:5-9; Exodus 25:30).

decisions.choice: the house of God: the tabernacle, then at Nob
decisions.reason: The temple had not yet been built. The tent of meeting stood at Nob (1 Samuel 21:1).

decisions.choice: they ate, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: he ate, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "he ate". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: statements instead of a question
decisions.reason: The verse continues the question of 12:3. Balanced and Readable tell the story as statements so it is easy to follow.

source.text: ἢ οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι τοῖς σάββασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τὸ σάββατον βεβηλοῦσιν καὶ ἀναίτιοί εἰσιν;

records.literal_gloss: Or not have you read in the law that on the Sabbaths the priests in the temple the Sabbath profane and guiltless are?

en.L: Or have you not read in the law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?
en.B: Or have you not read in the law that every Sabbath the priests working in the temple break the Sabbath, and still they bear no guilt?
en.R: And have you not read in the Law of Moses that the priests work in the temple on the Sabbath? They break the Sabbath rules, but God does not count them guilty.

fr.L: Ou bien n’avez-vous pas lu dans la Loi que, le jour du sabbat, les prêtres dans le temple profanent le sabbat et sont innocents ?
fr.B: Ou n’avez-vous pas lu dans la Loi que, chaque sabbat, les prêtres qui servent dans le temple violent le sabbat sans être coupables pour autant ?
fr.R: Et vous n’avez pas lu dans la Loi de Moïse que les prêtres travaillent dans le temple le jour du sabbat ? Ils ne respectent pas les règles du sabbat, mais Dieu ne les considère pas comme coupables.

decisions.choice: the priests' Sabbath work: the offerings and the holy bread
decisions.reason: The law required extra offerings on the Sabbath (Numbers 28:9-10), and the holy bread was set out every Sabbath (Leviticus 24:8). The priests worked so that this could be done.

decisions.choice: profane: treat as ordinary, by doing work the day otherwise forbids
decisions.reason: The priests do not despise the Sabbath. They do on it what would be work on any other day.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: God does not count them guilty
decisions.reason: Readable says who holds them innocent: the law God gave.

decisions.choice: le temple at every level, here and in 12:6
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "la cour du temple" at Balanced and Readable for scenes in the outer courts. Here the priests' service and the comparison in 12:6 concern the sanctuary as a whole, so "le temple" is the right word at every level, as in the English.

source.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦ ἱεροῦ μεῖζόν ἐστιν ὧδε.

records.literal_gloss: I say but to you that the temple greater is here.

en.L: But I tell you that [something] greater than the temple is here.
en.B: I tell you, here is something greater than the temple.
en.R: But I tell you, something more important than the temple is here with you now.

fr.L: Or je vous dis que [quelque chose de] plus grand que le temple est ici.
fr.B: Je vous le dis : il y a ici plus grand que le temple.
fr.R: Mais je vous le dis : il y a ici, avec vous, quelque chose de plus important que le temple.

decisions.choice: something greater: the word is neuter
decisions.reason: The neuter points to Jesus and what God is doing through him, which is greater than the temple and its service. If priests serving the temple are guiltless, so are those who serve him.

decisions.choice: here with you now
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "here" means in their presence.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν· Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν, οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους.

records.literal_gloss: If but you had known what is, Mercy I desire and not sacrifice, not would you have condemned the guiltless.

en.L: But if you had understood what this is, 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned those who are guiltless.
en.B: If you had understood what the words mean, 'I want mercy, not sacrifice,' you would not have condemned people who have done nothing wrong.
en.R: The Scriptures say, 'I want you to show mercy to people, more than I want you to offer sacrifices.' If you had understood what that means, you would not have judged these innocent men to be guilty.

fr.L: Mais si vous aviez compris ce que signifie : “Je veux la miséricorde, et non le sacrifice”, vous n’auriez pas condamné ceux qui sont innocents.
fr.B: Si vous aviez compris le sens de ces paroles : “Ce que je veux, c’est la miséricorde, non le sacrifice”, vous n’auriez pas condamné des gens qui n’ont rien fait de mal.
fr.R: Les Écritures disent : “Je veux que vous ayez pitié des autres, plus que je ne veux que vous m’offriez des sacrifices.” Si vous aviez compris ce que cela veut dire, vous n’auriez pas déclaré coupables ces hommes innocents.

decisions.choice: I desire mercy, not sacrifice: Hosea 6:6, quoted already in 9:13
decisions.reason: God wants faithful love more than offerings. The "not" ranks the two. The wording is kept the same as in 9:13 at each level.

decisions.choice: the guiltless: the disciples
decisions.reason: The same word described the priests in 12:5. The disciples are as innocent as they are.

decisions.choice: the quotation first, then the condition
decisions.reason: Readable gives the Scripture before saying what they failed to understand.

source.text: κύριος γάρ ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: Lord for is of the Sabbath the Son of the Man.

en.L: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
en.B: For the Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath."
en.R: The Son of Man is the Lord who rules over the Sabbath day."

fr.L: Car le Fils de l’homme est Seigneur du sabbat. »
fr.B: Oui, le Fils de l’homme est Seigneur du sabbat. »
fr.R: Le Fils de l’homme est le Seigneur qui a autorité sur le sabbat. »

decisions.choice: Lord of the Sabbath: Jesus has authority over the day God gave
decisions.reason: God made the Sabbath holy (Exodus 20:8-11). The Son of Man has the right to say what the day allows.

decisions.choice: Lord: placed first in the sentence for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "Lord" at the head of the sentence.

source.text: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτῶν·

records.literal_gloss: And having moved on from there he came into the synagogue of them;

en.L: And moving on from there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into their synagogue.
en.B: Jesus left that place and went into their synagogue.
en.R: Then Jesus went on from there and entered their synagogue, the place where people met to worship.

fr.L: Et, étant parti de là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} alla dans leur synagogue.
fr.B: Jésus quitta cet endroit et entra dans leur synagogue.
fr.R: Puis Jésus est parti de là et il est entré dans leur synagogue, l’endroit où les gens se réunissaient pour adorer Dieu.

decisions.choice: their synagogue: the synagogue of the people of that place
alternatives: a synagogue belonging to the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Matthew often says "their synagogues" (4:23; 9:35). The Pharisees of 12:2 are present there (12:14).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος χεῖρα ἔχων ξηράν.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, a man a hand having withered.

en.L: And look, [there was] a man having a withered hand.
en.B: A man was there whose hand was shriveled.
en.R: There was a man there with a hand that was shriveled and useless.

fr.L: Et voici, [il y avait là] un homme qui avait une main desséchée.
fr.B: Il s’y trouvait un homme dont la main était desséchée.
fr.R: Il y avait là un homme qui avait une main toute sèche ; il ne pouvait plus s’en servir.

decisions.choice: withered: dried up and shrunken, so that it could not be used
decisions.reason: The word means dry. It is used of a hand that cannot move (1 Kings 13:4).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Εἰ ἔξεστι τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύειν;

records.literal_gloss: And they asked him saying, If it is lawful on the Sabbaths to heal?

en.L: And they questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"
en.B: They put a question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Is healing allowed on the Sabbath?"
en.R: Some Pharisees were there. They asked Jesus, "Does our law allow anyone to heal on the Sabbath?"

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogèrent, disant : « Est-il permis de guérir le jour du sabbat ? »
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} posèrent cette question : « Est-il permis de guérir quelqu’un le jour du sabbat ? »
fr.R: Il y avait aussi des Pharisiens. Ils ont demandé à Jésus : « Est-ce que notre Loi permet de guérir quelqu’un le jour du sabbat ? »

decisions.choice: if: here it introduces a direct question
decisions.reason: In the Greek of this time the word for "if" can begin a question.

decisions.choice: healing on the Sabbath: debated
alternatives: clearly forbidden by the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The law of Moses does not mention healing on the Sabbath. Later Jewish teaching allowed it when a life was in danger; this man's life was not.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: Some Pharisees
decisions.reason: The questioners are the Pharisees, as 12:14 shows. Readable names them.

source.text: ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: so that they might accuse him.

en.L: so that they might accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They wanted a reason to bring a charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They were hoping to find a reason to accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: afin de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.
fr.B: Ils cherchaient un motif pour porter une accusation contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Ils espéraient trouver une raison de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.

decisions.choice: accuse: bring a formal charge
decisions.reason: The verb is used of bringing a charge before judges. Breaking the Sabbath was a serious offense under the law (Exodus 31:14).

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίς ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἕξει πρόβατον ἕν, καὶ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ τοῦτο τοῖς σάββασιν εἰς βόθυνον, οὐχὶ κρατήσει αὐτὸ καὶ ἐγερεῖ;

records.literal_gloss: He but said to them, What man will be of you who will have sheep one, and if falls this on the Sabbaths into a pit, not will take hold of it and raise?

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "What {{gender:person|man}} will there be among you who has one sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift [it] out?
en.B: He answered them, "Suppose one of you has just one sheep, and it falls into a hole on the Sabbath. Will you not grab hold of it and pull it out?
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Suppose one of you has only one sheep, and it falls into a deep hole on the Sabbath. You will surely grab it and pull it out.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Qui d’entre vous, ayant une seule brebis, si elle tombe dans une fosse le jour du sabbat, ne la saisira pas et ne la relèvera pas ?
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Supposons que l’un de vous n’ait qu’une seule brebis et qu’elle tombe dans un trou le jour du sabbat. Ne va-t-il pas la saisir et l’en sortir ?
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Imaginez que l’un de vous a une seule brebis, et qu’elle tombe dans un trou profond le jour du sabbat. Vous allez sûrement l’attraper et la sortir de là.

decisions.choice: rescuing an animal on the Sabbath: what his hearers would do
alternatives: a rule all Jews agreed on
decisions.reason: Jewish groups disagreed about this. The Damascus Document found at Qumran forbids lifting an animal out of a pit on the Sabbath. Jesus appeals to what his hearers themselves would do.

decisions.choice: one sheep: perhaps the only one the man owns
alternatives: one sheep out of a flock
decisions.reason: The number stresses how much the loss would matter to him.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: Will you not lift it out?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Readable gives the answer.

decisions.choice: Qui d’entre vous (L), with no gender span
decisions.reason: English Literal puts "person / man" under the gender setting. French says the same idiom with the generic pronoun "qui d’entre vous", which already means anyone and so takes no span (style guide §7).

source.text: πόσῳ οὖν διαφέρει ἄνθρωπος προβάτου.

records.literal_gloss: By how much then is worth more a man than a sheep.

en.L: How much more valuable then is a human being than a sheep!
en.B: And a human being is worth far more than a sheep!
en.R: And a person is worth much more than a sheep!

fr.L: Combien donc un être humain vaut-il plus qu’une brebis !
fr.B: Or un être humain vaut bien plus qu’une brebis !
fr.R: Et une personne vaut beaucoup plus qu’une brebis !

decisions.choice: an exclamation, from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates it as a statement. If a sheep may be rescued, how much more a person (6:26; 10:31).

source.text: ὥστε ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν καλῶς ποιεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: So that it is lawful on the Sabbaths well to do.

en.L: So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath."
en.B: So the law allows doing good on the Sabbath."
en.R: So the law allows people to do good things on the Sabbath."

fr.L: Ainsi, il est permis de faire du bien le jour du sabbat. »
fr.B: La Loi permet donc de faire du bien le jour du sabbat. »
fr.R: La Loi permet donc de faire de bonnes choses le jour du sabbat. »

decisions.choice: to do good: to act rightly and help others
decisions.reason: The phrase means to do what is right and kind, here by healing.

decisions.choice: on the Sabbath: one Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The Greek often uses the plural for a single Sabbath day.

source.text: τότε λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη.

records.literal_gloss: Then he says to the man, Stretch out of you the hand; and he stretched out, and it was restored healthy as the other.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched [it] out, and it was restored, healthy like the other.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held it out, and it was made well again, just like his other hand.
en.R: Then Jesus said to the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held out his hand, and it became healthy again. It was just like his other hand.

fr.L: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme : « Étends ta main. » Et il [l’]étendit, et elle fut rendue saine comme l’autre.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme : « Tends la main. » L’homme la tendit, et elle redevint saine, tout comme l’autre.
fr.R: Puis Jésus a dit à l’homme : « Tends la main. » L’homme a tendu la main, et elle est redevenue saine. Elle était exactement comme son autre main.

decisions.choice: it was restored: God's work through Jesus's word
decisions.reason: Jesus heals by a word alone. The passive points to God as the one who restores.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: ἐξελθόντες δὲ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone out but the Pharisees counsel took against him how him they might destroy.

en.L: But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, how they might destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Pharisees left and met together to plot against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, looking for a way to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death.
en.R: Then the Pharisees went out and met together. They made plans to kill Jesus.

fr.L: Mais les Pharisiens, étant sortis, tinrent conseil contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sur la manière de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire périr.
fr.B: Les Pharisiens sortirent et se réunirent pour comploter contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ; ils cherchaient un moyen de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir.
fr.R: Alors les Pharisiens sont sortis et se sont réunis. Ils ont fait des plans pour tuer Jésus.

decisions.choice: destroy: kill
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Herod seeking to kill the child Jesus (2:13). This is the first plot against Jesus's life by the leaders.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς γνοὺς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus having known withdrew from there.

en.L: But Jesus, knowing [it], withdrew from there.
en.B: Jesus knew what they were planning, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} withdrew from there.
en.R: Jesus knew about their plan, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place.

fr.L: Mais Jésus, l’ayant su, se retira de là.
fr.B: Jésus sut ce qu’ils préparaient, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se retira de là.
fr.R: Jésus a appris ce qu’ils voulaient faire. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est parti de cet endroit.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away from danger
decisions.reason: Matthew uses this verb when Jesus or his family moves away from a threat (2:14, 22; 4:12; 14:13).

decisions.choice: what they were planning (B); about their plan (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Jesus knew.

source.text: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς πάντας, καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιήσωσιν, ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·

records.literal_gloss: And followed him many, and he healed them all, \v 16 and he warned them that not known him they should make, \v 17 so that might be fulfilled the spoken through Isaiah the prophet saying,

en.L: And many followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them all, \v 16 and warned them that they should not make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known, \v 17 so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
en.B: Many people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed every one of them. \v 16 But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered them not to tell others who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was. \v 17 This was so that the word spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled:
en.R: Many people followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed all of them. \v 16 But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} warned them not to tell anyone about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 17 This made what the prophet Isaiah had said come true:

fr.L: Et beaucoup {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit tous, \v 16 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ordonna sévèrement de ne pas {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire connaître, \v 17 afin que s’accomplisse ce qui avait été dit par le prophète Isaïe, qui disait :
fr.B: Beaucoup de gens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivirent, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit tous. \v 16 Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ordonna de ne pas dire aux autres qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était. \v 17 Il en fut ainsi pour que s’accomplisse la parole annoncée par le prophète Isaïe :
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont suivi, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a tous guéris. \v 16 Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a ordonné de ne parler de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à personne. \v 17 Ainsi, ce que le prophète Isaïe avait dit s’est réalisé :

decisions.choice: not to make him known: Jesus does not seek fame
alternatives: he wanted to keep the healings secret from the Pharisees only
decisions.reason: Matthew explains the command by the quotation that follows: God's servant does not shout or push himself forward (12:19).

decisions.choice: many, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: many crowds, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "many crowds". The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the same wording as 8:17
decisions.reason: The formula that introduces a fulfilled prophecy is given in the same words each time.

decisions.choice: Isaïe
decisions.reason: "Isaïe" is the form of general French usage, used throughout this translation's French; "Ésaïe" is the Protestant form.

source.text: Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα, ὁ ἀγαπητός μου εἰς ὃν εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· θήσω τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ κρίσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπαγγελεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: Behold the servant of me whom I chose, the beloved of me in whom was well pleased the soul of me; I will put the Spirit of me upon him, and justice to the Gentiles he will proclaim.

en.L: "Look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant whom I have chosen, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} beloved in whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul is well pleased; I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will proclaim justice to the Gentiles.
en.B: "See {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, the one I have chosen, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved one, in whom {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul delights. I will place {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make justice known to the Gentiles.
en.R: "Here is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant. I have chosen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He will announce justice to people of every nation.

fr.L: « Voici {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, que j’ai choisi, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} bien-aimé, en qui {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} âme a pris plaisir ; je mettrai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Esprit sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} annoncera la justice aux nations.
fr.B: « Voici {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur, celui que j’ai choisi, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} bien-aimé, en qui {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} âme trouve sa joie. Je placerai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Esprit sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera connaître la justice aux non-Juifs.
fr.R: « Voici {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur. Je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai choisi. Je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aime, et je suis très content de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Je mettrai {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Esprit sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il annoncera la justice aux gens de toutes les nations.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 42:1-4: the servant of the LORD
alternatives: a general saying about God's people
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes the passage in a form of his own, close to neither the Hebrew nor the Greek Old Testament throughout. Where Isaiah has "my chosen", Matthew has "my beloved", the word of the voice at Jesus's baptism (3:17; see 17:5).

decisions.choice: servant: the servant of God in Isaiah
decisions.reason: The word can mean child or servant. Isaiah's servant is meant, and Matthew sees him in Jesus.

decisions.choice: justice: the right order God establishes
decisions.reason: The word can mean judgment. In Isaiah 42 it is the just rule the servant brings, even to the nations.

decisions.choice: spans on "my" for God and on "he" and "him" for the servant
decisions.reason: God speaks here, and the servant is Jesus, so the pronouns for both take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: look (L), here is (B, R); Gentiles (L, B), people of every nation (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced introduces the servant as a herald would. Readable says who the Gentiles are.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); les gens de toutes les nations (R), here and in 12:21
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms: Literal keeps the word "nations", Balanced says "non-Juifs" where the English says "Gentiles", and Readable follows the English "people of every nation". "Les païens" would say "pagans", a judgment the word does not carry here.

source.text: οὐκ ἐρίσει οὐδὲ κραυγάσει, οὐδὲ ἀκούσει τις ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Not will he quarrel nor cry out, nor will hear anyone in the streets the voice of him.

en.L: He will not quarrel nor shout, nor will anyone hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice in the broad streets.
en.B: He will not quarrel or shout; no one will hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} raising {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice in the streets.
en.R: He will not argue with people or shout at them. No one will hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} shouting in the streets.

fr.L: Il ne se querellera pas et ne criera pas, et personne n’entendra {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} voix dans les grandes rues.
fr.B: Il ne cherchera pas querelle, il ne criera pas ; personne ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendra élever la voix dans les rues.
fr.R: Il ne se disputera pas avec les gens et ne criera pas contre eux. Personne ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}entendra crier dans les rues.

decisions.choice: quarrel, cry out: the servant does not fight or push himself forward
decisions.reason: Matthew sees this in Jesus's withdrawal and his command not to make him known (12:15-16).

decisions.choice: the streets: the wide, public streets of a town
decisions.reason: The word means the broad streets where people gathered and speakers drew crowds.

source.text: κάλαμον συντετριμμένον οὐ κατεάξει καὶ λίνον τυφόμενον οὐ σβέσει, ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν.

records.literal_gloss: A reed bruised not he will break and a wick smoldering not he will quench, until he brings out to victory the justice.

en.L: A crushed reed {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not break, and a smoldering wick {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not put out, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings justice forth to victory.
en.B: He will not snap off a bent reed or snuff out a wick that is barely burning, until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has led justice on to victory.
en.R: He will not break off a reed that is bent. He will not put out a lamp wick that is barely burning. He will be like this until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes justice win.

fr.L: Le roseau broyé, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne le brisera pas, et la mèche qui fume, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne l’éteindra pas, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} mène la justice à la victoire.
fr.B: Il ne cassera pas le roseau plié, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’éteindra pas la mèche qui brûle à peine, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ait conduit la justice à la victoire.
fr.R: Il ne cassera pas un roseau qui est plié. Il n’éteindra pas la mèche d’une lampe qui brûle à peine. Il agira ainsi jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fasse triompher la justice.

decisions.choice: the crushed reed and the smoldering wick: people who are weak and failing
decisions.reason: The servant does not finish off those who are bent or almost spent. He is gentle with them (see 11:28-29).

decisions.choice: until he brings justice to victory: Isaiah 42:3-4 in brief
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the servant will bring out justice faithfully and not grow faint until he has set justice in the earth. Matthew sums this up.

decisions.choice: victory: success, the final triumph of justice
decisions.reason: The servant's gentleness is not weakness; justice will win in the end.

decisions.choice: He will be like this until
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence and joins the last clause to what comes before.

source.text: καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And in the name of him Gentiles will hope.

en.L: And in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name [the] Gentiles will hope."
en.B: And the Gentiles will put their hope in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name."
en.R: People of every nation will put their hope in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

fr.L: Et en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom les nations espéreront. »
fr.B: Et les non-Juifs mettront leur espérance en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom. »
fr.R: Les gens de toutes les nations mettront leur espoir en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »

decisions.choice: the Gentiles will hope in his name: Isaiah 42:4 in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Here Matthew follows the Greek Old Testament. The Hebrew says the coastlands will wait for his teaching.

decisions.choice: his name: the servant himself, all that he is
decisions.reason: To hope in someone's name is to hope in that person.

decisions.choice: in him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.
